Break in Men: Burglar Proof Holiday story

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We ask experts and a convicted house intruder how they choose which homes to enter and give tips on how to help you safe guard your homes.

Unique Selling Point:
So what makes one house on a street a target, while the other isn't? Well ex Naval Intelligence officer Renford Brand and his Intrusion prevention company, as well as expert Prof Rudolph Zinn are going to help our audience understand the minds of the criminal - why they choose a house, and how they look for weaknesses. As a preventative story, we will have several scenarios with a presenter where we go pick out houses with the convicted burglar and experts and they say why they would pick one over the other, we will also have mac doing some of the tasks set by the guys to him to maximize his energy and interactions.

Summary:
MORE INFO ON RENFORD: I am an ex SAPS officer with 12 years’ service in CID, followed by 22 years as senior officer in Naval Counter Intelligence, resigned to establish Independent Security Consultancy (ISC). You may not remember me (the chap with one leg) - we chatted at the lecture you presented in UCT end 2010 which I found very informative. I read your book on home intrusions that you kindly signed for me. One of the most informative pieces of crime intelligence I have read. I also make use of the ISS website. An integral part of the Risk and Vulnerability Analysis conducted by us, is to perform Intrusion Tests at sites as we believe that knowing and understanding criminal modus operandi provides one with the basis for further security planning, Tests without which the Security Plan and any subsequent measures implemented, will be flawed. As an example please view YouTube https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ketzgzyqrpo. and attached photos of intrusion tests. All electric fences were fully powered at the time. Professional criminals and syndicates can collect this info from other sources and most amateur intruders know it and are experienced at it. I believe this common knowledge, and available on media, including YouTube in many forms, hiding these tactics from public helps no one, showing these tactics changes nothing for the criminal but may sway the ordinary citizen to make improvements. These tests highlight the shortcomings with many typical ‘target hardening;’ approaches and the burgeoning private security industry whereby those involved are not adequately trained or experienced to provide advice. We are totally independent and don’t promote any products or services. Our concern is to ensure the correct design, solution and implementation of planned security measures in order to mitigate vulnerabilities and intrusions. We have over 40 years’ experience in this! For an overview of ISC please take a moment to visit www.iscafrica.co.za

Further information:
professor zinn says: Dr. Rudolph Zinn from UNISA’s School of Criminal Justice conducted research into understanding and preventing house robbery in South Africa. Based on in-depth interviews with convicted robbers, this is what he found:

8 out of 10 residential robberies are committed with the help of information from maids, gardeners and former employees.

Robbers will monitor the home for as long as two weeks.
Most attacks occur between 19:00 and midnight as people are relaxed, sleeping, cooking or watching TV and the security systems and beams are not activated. Robberies can continue until 04:00.
97% of robbers are armed.
On average, an armed robbery gang has four members.
The average age of a house robber is 19 to 26 years of age.
An average of 30% of all house robbers have either committed murder, or won’t hesitate to commit murder.
Only 17% of house robbers are foreigners.
Of all arrested robbers, 90% had no matric qualification or were unemployed. The 10% who had been employed gave up their jobs when confirming how much they could ‘earn’ from a robbery.
Most victims or targets are affluent persons who openly display their wealth, for example wearing expensive jewellery.
The average robber commits 103 robberies over 7 years before getting caught.
Most attackers’ homes or ‘bases’ are a 10 to 30 minute drive from the target address.
The conviction rate for house robberies in South Africa is only 7.67%. In the USA it is 53%.
Robbers are not deterred by alarms and armed reaction services.
These security measures are a major deterrent to crime:
Electric fences
Detection beams
Closed Circuit Television (CCTV)
Small dogs that sleep inside the house (robbers consider this to be the biggest deterrent of all.)
In the words of Dr Rudolph Zinn from his book Home Invasion – “They scout a neighbourhood to see how tight the security is. A patrol or neighbourhood watch factors in 68% on whether they go in or not, so having a good neighbourhood watch in the area can be a major deterrent.”
Stay safe. Find out more about RRVA membership.

Before you leave your house…
Make sure all shrubs and trees are trimmed back so that they do not allow a burglar to conceal himself while attempting to open a window or door. If possible, plant bushes with prickly thorns around these locations.

Don’t stop your security awareness at the outside walls of your house. Your yard areas (if any) also deserve attention. In general, don’t leave anything around the yard that might help a burglar get into your house. Ladders, stackable boxes or any garden tools should be put away, preferably in a locked cabinet. Many burglars have used the property owner’s own tools to break into a home.

Don’t place outdoor furniture tables nearby the house, as these could become an easy stepladder to the roof. Rather move them inside in the evening.

Second-story windows are often left unsecured, making it easy for the criminal to get into the house. To discourage potential climbers, spread grease on any metal drainpipes if they are close to windows. Use Vaseline or clear automotive grease, depending on the colour of the pipe (or replace with plastic pipe).

A barking dog, changing your daily routine and the presence of CCTV cameras could make your home a less attractive target to criminals.
Make sure your post box is always empty. A full post box makes it seem like you are never home.
Since robbers can watch your movements for as long as two weeks, try to deviate from your usual routine regularly. Leave and return home at different times, use different routes and visit different shops to what you typically do.

Take extreme care when hiring domestic workers and other service providers cannot be underestimated. Be careful who you let into your home.

Press Release:


INTRO: 300000 burglaries are reported annually in South Africa, meaning the biggest threat to citizens is burglary. We spoke with a former intelligence officer in the navy, who protected borders and assets and is now protecting homes by identifying your security’s weaknesses by actually breaking in - this is called intrusion testing. A study conducted over the past 18 months which interviewed prisoners convicted of burglary and robberies has preventative information on how to protect homes and lives. Mac finds out that you always have to be on your guard.

Script:


Crime trends annually show a remarkable spike in burglaries over the festive season. George, not his real name, is a reformed career burglar who operated in a syndicate and was in and out of jail for 10 years. Agile, he enters this house within 60 seconds...catching, even me, unaware. (mac looks surprised)
Mac: So george you’re saying that actually having furniture around like this this is paradise for you?
G: you can get up the better you just pop things on top of each other, easy movable
Mac: how fast do you need to be to be able to do this?
G: yeah you move quite quick you don’t think about it, you just climb you get used to it, The quicker the better
(He quickly shows us)
Mac: jeez im not going to try that though hahah
George is emparting his experience and knowledge to protect citizens' homes but also their lives.
SO THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROGRAM IS NOT TO EDUCATE vTHE CRIMINAL BECAUSE THIS IS STUFF THEY ALREADY KNOW, BUT ITS TO EDUCATE YOU TOO.
George’s skill set is exactly what veteran independent security consultant Renford Brand uses to test a home’s intrusion points.
Brand: I find out that the obvious thing to do, because of my operational background was actually to test the systems and do intrusions which is the quickest way of identifying weaknesses
As a former intelligence officer in the Navy, he protected South Africa’s national borders and assets.
Mac: so you went from protecting the country and securing national key points to protecting teddy bears, cars and families? (laugh)
Brand: it became a passion of mine particularly with the security of homes and indiv and estates where it’s a bit more personal.
Zinn: If you look at the crime stats, the biggest threat to people in South Africa is burglary.
Former police officer Professor Rudoph Zinn lectures at UNISA in the department of police practice and specialises in acts of violent crime. He’s interviewed hundreds of incarcerated offenders who provided advice on how to deter home invaders.
Zinn: they call it the University of the Underworld, if you go into prison, you are astonished to find out how intelligent they are, the ability to to plan properly.
The difference between a burglar and a robber, is that a burglar wants to get in and out quickly, whereas a robber plans to stay at the house for a longer period, and is willing to resort to violence.
Brand: you get your amateur, your opportunist, and your syndicates to mitigate the risks one needs to have a layered security system in place.
Our research looks at commonly used methods to deter criminals to see how effective they are.
Become active in local neighborhood watch groups.
Zinn: when the burglars and robbers decide they need to go to a specific area, look at access control, look at visible security. That place a 68 percent deterrent factor for them, whether they would actually go to another neighborhood or concentrate on this one specific one.
Choose homes on street corners not in dead ends or the middle of the block.
Zinn: It’s easier here to commit a burglary than on the street corner itself because here they can see people approaching.
Studies show fences are better because walls help the criminals remain undetected for longer.
Zinn: I haven't ever seen a fence that could not be breached. So fences are not there to keep them out. its very difficult for them to get over a fence like this with the unstable top. This is not sturdy so its very difficult to stabilize and get over. this is a typical step ladder that they would be able to step on and climb over.
High walls and fences can actually attract criminals.
Mac: is there anything specific that would make you pick one house over another?
G: sometimes you look for the most secured fencing, secured house because you think there’s more valuables inside of that house, than the house that is just easy to jump over, one has money, the other doesn’t have money
Mac: so renford you say there is an alternative way of securing your house and of going a bit green?
Brand: you can have a very good barrier in the form of different types of thorny hedges. This is called a bougainvillea you wont get through this without a tremendous amount of pain
Electric fences aren’t lethal, so at worst a criminal could just endure the shock and jump over.
SO THIS IS AN ELECTRIC FENCE, MOST HOUSES HAVE THEM AND THINK THEY’RE SECURE, THIS ABOUT 9000VOLTS BUT LET ME GIVE YOU SOME SHOCKING NEWS, YOU PROBABLY THINK THAT ITS A DETERRENT LETS FIND OUT IF GEORGE CAN GET OVER IT HOW SAFE YOU ARE.
And just like that he’s over the fence within seconds.
Brand: preferably at an angle slightly out (mac shows him out like that) otherwise the height, is the most important thing, but its an advantage to be at an angle out there.
Ensure gates have a stopper preventing them from being lifted.
Zinn: 2-3 of them lift it off of the track and then just walk open the gate. So this is what you need to do to prevent this.
Contrary to popular belief CCTV cameras aren’t a deterrent, but play a role in collecting evidence after an incident.
SO NOWADAYS THINGS HAVE GOTTEN SO SOPHISTICATED THAT A CAMERA LIKE THIS – YOU CAN TALK THROUGH IT, YOU CAN SEE, AND YOU CAN HEAR WHATS HAPPENING AND WITH SOMETHING LIKE THIS YOU CAN USE THE WORLD FAMOUS SOUTH AFRICAN DETERRENT “VOETSAK” WHILE HE’S TRYING TO JUMP OVER.
Install different kinds of beams, bright lights and connect these to alarm systems. Criminals don’t want attention.
Zinn: Anything like this that would pick up movement, this would attract the attention of the people inside the house even if you walk slowly it should pick you up.
Disguise beams and ensure they aren’t visible like this. Bright lights and noisy alarms as shown here are definite deterrents.
Brand: this is a screamer
Mac: how much does one of these costs?
Brand: R150 bucks.
Small yappy dogs kept inside the house are actually more of a deterrent than dogs kept outside which can be easily overcome or poisoned.
Z: They explained it saying at the time the crime was to take place. When people are awake inside the house in the morning, five to seven in the afternoon, five to 11 people have been switched on the alarm system as yet. So there's nothing that can be a pre warning system. And they the dog inside the house with an alert to somebody that's an intruder outside.
Burglars often look for easy access points like doors and windows without burglar bars.
Mac: And then a window like this would you be able to get into one of these?
G: Just use a screwdriver.
Mac: And that’s it you’re in already
Mac: how safe is this?
G: It’s not as safe as I think it could be, you can take the spade and open the door just pop the door open
MAC TRIES: From here to there, oh actually I could break in here
George: you can use the spade like a stepping ladder, so you don’t have to struggle and you can see it’s like week, you can actually pop this open with you fingers
Mac: Don’t leave a spade or any tools in your back yard, its not a good idea.
Mac: So what about the bricks and walls of a house help in anyway?
George: yeah of course its like climbing, you can grip on it, step on it, the smoother the better obviously because you can’t (shows feet movement)
Have a predetermined ‘safe room’ with access to a panic button or phone. If you cannot get there in time DO NOT be confrontational.
Zinn: And they say the best that I can say is if you once you are faced with a firearm, don't do anything that is going to simulate self-defense. They are willing to use lethal force. if they are able to get to the door of the house, and then only the loud sound, they would still commit the robbery.
The best defense is a layered and unexpected system that focuses on deterrence as early as possible.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We ask experts and a convicted house intruder how they choose which homes to enter and give tips on how to help you safe guard your homes.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: So what makes one house on a street a target, while the other isn't? Well ex Naval Intelligence officer Renford Brand and his Intrusion prevention company, as well as expert Prof Rudolph Zinn are going to help our audience understand the minds of the criminal - why they choose a house, and how they look for weaknesses. As a preventative story, we will have several scenarios with a presenter where we go pick out houses with the convicted burglar and experts and they say why they would pick one over the other, we will also have mac doing some of the tasks set by the guys to him to maximize his energy and interactions.
metadata.Summary: MORE INFO ON RENFORD: I am an ex SAPS officer with 12 years’ service in CID, followed by 22 years as senior officer in Naval Counter Intelligence, resigned to establish Independent Security Consultancy (ISC). You may not remember me (the chap with one leg) - we chatted at the lecture you presented in UCT end 2010 which I found very informative. I read your book on home intrusions that you kindly signed for me. One of the most informative pieces of crime intelligence I have read. I also make use of the ISS website. An integral part of the Risk and Vulnerability Analysis conducted by us, is to perform Intrusion Tests at sites as we believe that knowing and understanding criminal modus operandi provides one with the basis for further security planning, Tests without which the Security Plan and any subsequent measures implemented, will be flawed. As an example please view YouTube https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ketzgzyqrpo. and attached photos of intrusion tests. All electric fences were fully powered at the time. Professional criminals and syndicates can collect this info from other sources and most amateur intruders know it and are experienced at it. I believe this common knowledge, and available on media, including YouTube in many forms, hiding these tactics from public helps no one, showing these tactics changes nothing for the criminal but may sway the ordinary citizen to make improvements. These tests highlight the shortcomings with many typical ‘target hardening;’ approaches and the burgeoning private security industry whereby those involved are not adequately trained or experienced to provide advice. We are totally independent and don’t promote any products or services. Our concern is to ensure the correct design, solution and implementation of planned security measures in order to mitigate vulnerabilities and intrusions. We have over 40 years’ experience in this! metadata.Further information: professor zinn says: Dr. Rudolph Zinn from UNISA’s School of Criminal Justice conducted research into understanding and preventing house robbery in South Africa. Based on in-depth interviews with convicted robbers, this is what he found: 8 out of 10 residential robberies are committed with the help of information from maids, gardeners and former employees. Robbers will monitor the home for as long as two weeks. Most attacks occur between 19:00 and midnight as people are relaxed, sleeping, cooking or watching TV and the security systems and beams are not activated. Robberies can continue until 04:00. 97% of robbers are armed. On average, an armed robbery gang has four members. The average age of a house robber is 19 to 26 years of age. An average of 30% of all house robbers have either committed murder, or won’t hesitate to commit murder. Only 17% of house robbers are foreigners. Of all arrested robbers, 90% had no matric qualification or were unemployed. The 10% who had been employed gave up their jobs when confirming how much they could ‘earn’ from a robbery. Most victims or targets are affluent persons who openly display their wealth, for example wearing expensive jewellery. The average robber commits 103 robberies over 7 years before getting caught. Most attackers’ homes or ‘bases’ are a 10 to 30 minute drive from the target address. The conviction rate for house robberies in South Africa is only 7.67%. In the USA it is 53%. Robbers are not deterred by alarms and armed reaction services. These security measures are a major deterrent to crime: Electric fences Detection beams Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) Small dogs that sleep inside the house (robbers consider this to be the biggest deterrent of all.) In the words of Dr Rudolph Zinn from his book Home Invasion – “They scout a neighbourhood to see how tight the security is. A patrol or neighbourhood watch factors in 68% on whether they go in or not, so having a good neighbourhood watch in the area can be a major deterrent.” Stay safe. Find out more about RRVA membership. Before you leave your house… Make sure all shrubs and trees are trimmed back so that they do not allow a burglar to conceal himself while attempting to open a window or door. If possible, plant bushes with prickly thorns around these locations. Don’t stop your security awareness at the outside walls of your house. Your yard areas (if any) also deserve attention. In general, don’t leave anything around the yard that might help a burglar get into your house. Ladders, stackable boxes or any garden tools should be put away, preferably in a locked cabinet. Many burglars have used the property owner’s own tools to break into a home. Don’t place outdoor furniture tables nearby the house, as these could become an easy stepladder to the roof. Rather move them inside in the evening. Second-story windows are often left unsecured, making it easy for the criminal to get into the house. To discourage potential climbers, spread grease on any metal drainpipes if they are close to windows. Use Vaseline or clear automotive grease, depending on the colour of the pipe (or replace with plastic pipe). A barking dog, changing your daily routine and the presence of CCTV cameras could make your home a less attractive target to criminals. Make sure your post box is always empty. A full post box makes it seem like you are never home. Since robbers can watch your movements for as long as two weeks, try to deviate from your usual routine regularly. Leave and return home at different times, use different routes and visit different shops to what you typically do. Take extreme care when hiring domestic workers and other service providers cannot be underestimated. Be careful who you let into your home.
